reason: The cited evidence (E1, E2) describes LPBF processing and general solidification phenomena but provides no specific data or discussion on substrate preheating, its effect on cooling rates, segregation, residual stress, or defect reduction in AlCrFeNiSi or any similar alloy. The key premises are therefore unsupported by the cited passages.
premises: Substrate preheating at ~300°C reduces cooling rates and thermal gradients in LPBF
Reduced cooling rates enhance atomic diffusion and improve chemical homogeneity
Reduced thermal gradients lower residual stresses
Reduced cooling rates and stresses minimize defect formation (cracks, porosity)
These effects collectively improve mechanical integrity relative to conventional LPBF
